title: Day 26 — Agent Tool Dispatcher
prompt: An LLM agent emits tool calls like {tool, args}. This dispatcher looks up the tool and calls it, but it validates nothing — bad calls crash with raw errors. How would you make it robust?

clarifications.answer: An unknown tool name should raise ToolError (not a raw KeyError).
A tool declares its required params. Missing one should raise ToolError, not let the handler throw a TypeError.
Be strict: any argument the tool didn't declare should raise ToolError — don't silently pass it through.
A tool with no params called with empty args is valid.
Every invalid call should surface as one ToolError so the model gets a single predictable error to react to.
For this exercise validate presence of the right arg names (not their types) — existence, required, and no-extras.

hints: Treat the LLM as an untrusted caller: check everything before invoking the handler.
Three checks: tool in registry? required params all present? any unexpected keys? Each failure -> ToolError.
Compare set(args) against set(params): missing = required - given; extra = given - required.
